objective: Implement dreammusicforge/dmf_ir (schema, validator, models, compiler, tests) as the canonical, provider-neutral DMF-IR v1 source of truth, additive to the existing runtime.py baseline.

modifiedFiles.change: documented the second test-discovery command and the new DMF-IR test categories; did not alter the existing runtime.py test instructions

requiredTestsMapping.Kling provider compilation: DMFIRProviderNeutralCompilationTests in dreammusicforge/dmf_ir/tests/test_dmf_ir.py -- expressed provider-neutrally (the Continuity Compiler stage), plus test_runtime_still_validates_and_compiles_the_same_example re-running runtime.compile_kling_packages directly as a regression guard

newChecksBeyondRuntimePy: a continuity mode requiring a predecessor cannot appear on the first clip in the timeline
film.duration_seconds must match the last clip's end time
the music timeline must be contiguous (no gaps or overlaps) and must span the full film duration
a clip's source/destination reality-state timecodes must match the clip's own start/end
semantic and music events attached to a clip must actually overlap that clip's time window
required_reference_assets must resolve to a known character or world id
truthBoundary: This evidence proves deterministic schema/semantic validation and provider-neutral compilation against one worked example (begin_again_project.json), run twice (once through the existing runtime.py path, once through the new dmf_ir path) with identical acceptance results. It does not prove: real Kling API integration, real generated media, real frame/face/pose/lighting verification, or any of the not-yet-implemented compilers listed in the module roadmap. runtime.py is unmodified and still owns actual Kling package generation; dmf_ir is an additive, stricter canonical layer other compilers can build on, not yet the thing runtime.py itself consumes.
